category: D-RELEASE-1.0 §11 classification of every OPEN issue. Columns: issue, category, reason, owner. The gate scripts/check_release_blockers.sh cross-checks this ledger against the GitHub labels; drift is RED. Categories: 1.0-blocks | 1.0-outside | post-1.0 | not-a-bug | tracking/contract.

reason: Feature — reading text from documents (PDF/`documento.texto`); explicitly OUTSIDE the 0.5.0 scope and the 1.0 core surface, tracked under the official-packages plan (R1/interop-first, experimental). Real issue, accepted after 1.0.

Feature request (rule-6 decision) — `kof.io` has no `realPath`/reparse-point primitive: `isSymlink()` is false for a Windows directory junction, so a confinement check has no portable mechanism. New stdlib surface, outside the 1.0 core; registered as a DECISION REQUEST in `docs/development/README.md` §3.

Core JVM frontend soundness: an undeclared/unnamable type in a declaration (`Handle` used as a return type) passes `kof check` silently and the generated class fails at runtime with `NoClassDefFoundError: Handle`, while the same shape for `Result` is correctly refused `SEM011`. A compiler that accepts an unresolvable declared type and emits a broken class ref is a 1.0 blocker.

Docs bug — `learn/stdlib/process.md` and `docs/stdlib/shell.md` still say Native = `PROC001` while `process.run`, `shell.run/runWith/pipeline` and `process.spawn` are implemented on Native x86-64/riscv64/aarch64 (`docs/backend-parity.md` 25-26/09 + `ExpressionProcessCallLowerer`); only the MCU keeps `PROC001`. Docs-only correction, outside the 1.0 code surface.

Core JVM codegen: a user method named `get`/`post`/`put`/`patch`/`delete` called as a STATEMENT inside `try` emits invalid bytecode (`VerifyError: Inconsistent stackmap frames`) — the HTTP-verb name collides with the request-shape lowering. Real JVM backend correctness bug; 1.0 blocker.

Core contract violation: `kof.http` failures (connection refused, non-2xx) surface as raw Java exceptions (`java.net.ConnectException` / `IOException: HTTP 501`) that `catch (String e)` cannot see, contradicting the frozen "Kof throws Strings" contract (`learn/14-exceptions.md`); the program dies with no catch and no `after`. Implementation differs from the Kof contract = bug; 1.0 blocker.
